label: migration of an AI automation toolchain
context: A working system is already in use. The deliverable is a cutover that preserves what people depend on, not a parallel rewrite that never lands.

Context is a first-class artifact. Prompts, agent instructions, configuration, and documentation move in the same change as the code and tool upgrades they describe; a change that leaves them stale is incomplete.
Classify every legacy artifact before touching it: carried forward, translated to the new shape, or archived. Work that belonged to a retired lifecycle is archive, and porting it is waste.
Migrate by copy, verify against the legacy behaviour, then retire. Never mutate legacy state in place, and keep the old path readable until the new one is proven.
Tool and model upgrades change agent behaviour. State the CLI, version, and model contract a step assumes rather than inheriting whatever the legacy install happened to run.
Never carry credentials, keys, or absolute machine-local paths out of legacy configuration into new files, prompts, logs, or handoffs.
